note: One small primitive campground: a gravel loop about 55 m long in open oak timber on the east side of Highway 97, about 1.3 miles south of Highway 96, with metal fire rings and nothing else. MDC calls it best suited to tents or small travel trailers and RVs: the loop lane is narrow and there are no built pads. The rest of the area's lots are parking only. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: one designated campground (map symbol at lot 10 on Highway 97, one GIS point, a gravel loop on imagery). Free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit; phone matches. Pin is on the loop. MDC's 'best suited for tents or small travel trailers/RVs' wording flagged with a caveat in the note. The stored note's directions lead to the headquarters on Highway 96, not the campground - replaced.
flags: INCLUSION (stays - a built campground): the area page lists 'Camping: Individual Campsites' and says 'Camping is allowed only in the spot designated on the area map. No facilities are provided at the campground.' The brochure: 'Primitive camping is allowed only in campground designated on the area map ... All camping is first come-first served. No fires allowed except in metal firerings at the campground.' The map (09/14) draws exactly ONE Primitive Camping Area symbol, at parking lot 10 on Highway 97 on the west boundary; GIS layer 27 has one point (OBJECTID 5) at 37.17102,-93.94694 = the stored pin, with lot 1759 23 m west of it. On the leaf-off frame it is an oval gravel loop about 55 x 35 m entered straight off paved Highway 97, in open oak timber, lane about 3-4 m wide, no pads visible. So: how many - one campground, site count unpublished (a May 2025 Dyrt reviewer wrote 'only like five spots'); where - Highway 97, 2.1 km south of Highway 96; no other camping point anywhere on the 4,361 acres, so no cluster and no split. The page's bare 'Camping is prohibited.' after the Rule 140 text is the page artifact.

CRITERIA / RIG-LENGTH WORDING (singled out, no length stated): area page: 'The campground is best suited for tents or small travel trailers/RVs.' This is this area's own sentence, not MDC boilerplate. No length is posted. I found no review from the last 3 years in which a 23-ft+ rig is said to have fitted (the two Dyrt reviews, May 2025, state no rig; I did not read Campendium - its page redirected and I left it). On imagery the loop is a 55 x 35 m oval with a 3-4 m lane directly off a paved highway, which a 23-ft motorhome can drive; under the 2026-11-02 ruling (unclear pad size = keep with a caveat) I wrote the caveat into the note.

HORSE CAMP: none labelled. The map's five 'Horse Trailer Parking' lots (1, 7, 12, 15, 17) are separate symbols elsewhere on the area; lot 10 with the camping symbol is an ordinary Parking Lot. The campground is plainly a general camp.

GATE REPORT (secondary, not a status): thedyrt.com review dated May 4, 2025: 'When we got there we found a locked gate across the entrance to the conservation area! ... we ended up just sleeping in the parking lot'; review dated May 22, 2025: 'the first time there google maps were wrong ! So I drove around the block and found it. There is NO locked gate nice little spot'. MDC's page shows no closure. The stored directions ('From Stotts City, take Highway 97 north, then Highway 96 east 1 mile') are MDC's directions to the area headquarters, not the campground, which fits the first reviewer's experience - I took them out of the note and described where the loop is.
PIN: stored 37.17102,-93.94694 is the GIS point, on the south side of the loop. No move.
PHONE: stored 417-895-6880 matches the area page's 'For more information call (417) 895-6880'.
SEASON: stored year_round (manual) stands; brochure and page put no season on the campground (multi-use trails close for firearms deer season, not the camp).
